title: We're the bottleneck, but we don't have to be — Ido Salomon, AgentCraft
talk_summary: Ido Salomon demos AgentCraft, a game-inspired orchestrator that visualizes agents on a map, adds attention-jumping, autonomous task generation, review kits, and shared war rooms. The talk is mostly product demo and UX philosophy about human supervision being the bottleneck, with little measured engineering detail.

takeaways.technique: Review kit with visual evidence and parallel implementations
takeaways.what_they_do: Bundles all changes for review with per-file diffs plus screenshots/videos of what changed, and can run several implementations in parallel to pick the best.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can get just get visual evidence. So you can actually see videos of what changed or photos of what changed
go through my codebase, find out what the next things I need to do are, create these tasks for me and I just click a button

takeaways.what_they_do: A single prioritized view of which agent needs human attention, with a hotkey to jump to the nearest blocking item (approvals, plan sign-off).
takeaways.evidence_quote: you would click uh spacebar and it would just take you to the nearest thing that actually needed your attention

takeaways.technique: Shared war room with cross-agent notice board
takeaways.evidence_quote: there's also some kind of chat between not only between the people within the room, but also between agents

takeaways.what_they_do: Loops scan sources (GitHub, social) and auto-create feature work run in isolated containers without babysitting.
takeaways.evidence_quote: scan Twitter for cool stuff you want to build or scan your GitHub, and it will just create these nice uh features for you
